bottleneck: NGRAM greedy correctness remains BUG_CONFIRMED (canonical F1) with no promotion possible. The fault-line split is (A) verify-row context misalignment vs (B) post-commit KV/bonus misalignment. Prior CPU work on this branch: t4 excluded the accept-index/KV-move compaction given a valid tree root (root/convention audit in t3 statically refuted a stale-root path); t3 proved the tree-mask generator causal and its sanitize guard a no-op. The remaining unmodeled half of the verify input is the attention-mask assembly vs the KV read width: ngram_worker builds the prefix block of the custom mask from host seq_lens_cpu before the blocking sync, while ngram_info.generate_attn_arg_prefill derives per-row width from device paged_kernel_lens (+D) and silently pads a short mask with True. If those widths ever disagree, the whole per-request mask shifts and no assertion fires.
hypothesis: H-CPU-3 (new): the NGRAM verify custom-mask assembly in ngram_info.generate_attn_arg_prefill is algorithm-preserving (each draft row attends exactly prefix positions {0..p-1} union ancestor draft slots) if and only if the host prefix h_i used to build ones_masks equals the device prefix d_i used for the KV read width; any drift is silently absorbed by the append-True branch and corrupts every real row. Legitimate CUDA-graph batch padding (fake requests appended at the end) must still leave all real rows exact, so the recovery branch cannot be removed without distinguishing the two cases. Reachability of h_i != d_i is NOT claimed: the G3-i3 FutureMap audit argues host and device mirrors are equal by construction, so the primary expected outcome is a latent-hazard negative plus a decisive falsifier, not an F1 root cause.
patch: No engine change. New pure-stdlib CPU oracle ngram_oracle/mask_width_oracle.py + raw ngram_oracle/results/mask_width_oracle.json + write-up ngram_oracle/README-mask-width.md. It ports the width arithmetic of ngram_info.generate_attn_arg_prefill (row width = paged_kernel_lens + D with device seq_lens per flashinfer_backend 'paged_kernel_lens = seq_lens'; mask_numel = paged_kernel_lens_sum*D + D^2*bs; silent append-True when short) and the ones_masks prefix construction in ngram_worker.py:352-361 (host seq_lens_cpu width). Scenarios: consistent host/device on bfs and chain trees, host lags device by 1 and 2, host ahead by 1, and legitimate CUDA-graph batch padding with 2 fake requests. The existing ngram_oracle/topology_oracle.py (t4) and the t3 _sanitize_tree_mask guard are unchanged and not re-derived.
tests: Executed locally: python3 -I ngram_oracle/mask_width_oracle.py ngram_oracle/results/mask_width_oracle.json, exit 0, stdlib only, no GPU/provider/evaluator. Result: consistent_host_device PASS 12/12 real rows exact (bfs), consistent_host_device_chain PASS 12/12; graph_batch_padding PASS 12/12 real rows exact with 40 True entries appended only on fake rows; host_lags_device_k1 FAIL 0/12 (first mismatch req0 row0: extra column 8, missing column 4); host_lags_device_k2 FAIL 0/12; host_ahead_device_k1 FAIL 2/12. summary.consistent_pass=true, summary.mismatch_fails=true. No exception is raised in any drift scenario. NOT requested: no GPU/fast gate (request_fast_gate=false) because this trial ships no engine change to measure and a CPU negative is the deliverable; a fast screen of unchanged HEAD would not advance the NGRAM fault line. NOT_TESTED: real CUDA-graph padding mechanics, translator.pack_read_stream / assign_extend_cache_locs physical slot plan, flashinfer kernels, live overlap timing; h_i != d_i reachability on hardware.
learning: Bounded CPU negative finding, new component: the NGRAM verify mask assembly is exact iff host seq_lens_cpu (prefix block width) equals device paged_kernel_lens (KV read width) for every request; both tested tree shapes and legitimate graph batch padding are exact 12/12, so the assembly contract is sound under the documented FutureMap equality. The append-True recovery branch is not a padding-only path: a one-token host/device drift is silently consumed as real mask columns and corrupts 12/12 real rows with no assertion, which is exactly the kind of nondeterministic, batch/timing-dependent signature observed in the ON probe. However, reachability of a drift is NOT established (FutureMap audit argues against it; the observed first-diff positions 4/6 fit a persistent one-token width drift poorly), so this is a latent hazard and a falsifier, not the F1 root cause and not a fix. Limitations: pure index arithmetic; kernels, translator plan and target model were not executed; the JSON 'attended_padding_tail' field is structurally always false and is not used in any verdict; no numeric quality or performance claim is made.
next_proposal: Run the drift falsifier inside the existing batch-pinned ON/OFF NGRAM probe (512-token repeat prompts where divergence concentrates): a log-only counter at custom-mask construction that compares, per request, the host prefix used for ones_masks against the device paged_kernel_lens in the same forward, emitting requests-differing and total width delta to server.log. Decision rule: any non-zero drift on real requests -> width-drift class confirmed, then fix the host-mirror source and re-run the ALGORITHM_PRESERVING probe; zero drift with divergence reproduced -> width class excluded, and the remaining live GPU-visible surfaces are the physical KV-slot plan (pack_read_stream vs assign_extend_cache_locs) and the post-commit bonus/KV move, best attacked with the accept_lens==1 discriminator. Prefer bundling the counter with the existing correctness probe rather than consuming a fresh candidate slot; do not gate NGRAM on throughput until it is ALGORITHM_PRESERVING.
